Title: Register a unique customer, log in, and verify My profile
Preconditions: Browser on https://practicesoftwaretesting.com/. Tester is signed out. Use a unique email so this run cannot collide with other testers on the public SUT.
Steps:
1. Open https://practicesoftwaretesting.com/.
2. Click Sign in.
3. Click Register your account.
4. On Customer registration, enter First name, Last name, DOB (YYYY-MM-DD, 18+), Country, Postal code, House number (allow lookup to fill Street/City/State, or type them if lookup is slow), Phone, Email, and Password.
5. Click Register.
6. On Login, enter the same Email and Password; click Login.
7. Open the user menu and choose My profile.
8. Compare First name, Last name, and Email on Profile with the values from step 4.
TestData:
SUT: https://practicesoftwaretesting.com/
First name: Ava
Last name: Mercer
DOB: 1990-01-15
Country: Austria
Postal code: 1234AA
House number: 1
Phone: 1234567890
Email: user_{timestamp}@example.com (replace {timestamp} with a unique value, e.g. user_202608251430@example.com)
Password: Welcome1! (8+ characters, mixed case, number, symbol)
ExpectedResult:
After Register the tester is sent to Login and the message "Email is already in use." is not shown.
After Login the header shows the user menu (My account / My profile / My invoices / Sign out) instead of Sign in.
My profile displays the same first name, last name, and email used at registration.
ActualResult: 2026-08-26. Mapped to tests/ui/auth.spec.js @smoke unique customer can register, log in, and see matching profile. Passed.

Title: Add two different products to the cart
Preconditions: Home catalog. Cart must be empty: if a cart badge is already visible, open /checkout and use a fresh browser session (or clear site data) so leftover cart_id in sessionStorage is not reused. Login is optional for this case.
Steps:
1. Search Pliers, open Combination Pliers (or the first Pliers result), click Add to cart.
2. Return to the catalog (header home or Continue Shopping).
3. Search Hammer, open Thor Hammer (or the first Hammer result), click Add to cart.
4. Open the cart (header cart / /checkout step 1).
5. Read Item, Quantity, Price, and Total for each line.
TestData:
Product A: Combination Pliers (search: Pliers)
Product B: Thor Hammer (search: Hammer)
Quantity on add: default 1 for each
Do not update quantity in this case (that is TC-M-05).
ExpectedResult:
The cart lists two distinct product lines (Pliers and Hammer items).
Each line quantity is 1.
Line Price and cart Total equal the sum of both unit prices.
Proceed to checkout is available. The cart badge reflects 2 items.
Empty-cart copy "The cart is empty. Nothing to display." is not shown.
ActualResult: 2026-08-26. Mapped to tests/ui/purchase.spec.js @smoke @regression unique customer can search, update cart, checkout COD, and see invoice (two distinct cart lines). Passed.

Title: Cart quantity clamps below 1 and above 99
Preconditions: At least one product is in the cart (complete TC-M-04, or add Combination Pliers once). Cart page (/checkout step 1) is open. Note the unit price of the first line before changing quantity.
Steps:
1. On the first cart line, increase quantity to 2 (plus control or type 2 and leave the field). Confirm the line total equals unit price × 2 and the cart Total updates.
2. Change the quantity input to 0 and leave the field (Tab or click away). Do not expect the line to be deleted.
3. Change the quantity input to 100 and leave the field.
4. Read the quantity, line total, and any toast/warning.
TestData:
Starting product: Combination Pliers (or any in-cart line)
Qty after increase: 2
Qty under min: 0 (expect clamp to 1)
Qty over max: 100 (expect cap 99)
UI bounds: min 1, max 99
ExpectedResult:
After step 1, quantity is 2 and line total = unit price × 2.
After step 2, quantity is clamped to 1 (not 0, not removed). No error toast is required for 0.
After step 3, quantity is capped at 99 and a warning toast is shown. Line total = unit price × 99.
Unbounded quantity 100 is not kept.
ActualResult: 2026-08-26. Mapped to tests/ui/cart.spec.js @regression cart quantity clamps below 1 and above 99. Passed.

Title: Complete Cash on Delivery checkout with Confirm twice
Preconditions: Logged in as the unique customer from TC-M-01 (do not use Continue as Guest — guest has no My invoices). Cart contains at least one product from TC-M-04. If TC-M-05 left a line at quantity 99, set that line back to 1 before Proceed so this checkout is not a 99-unit order. Billing fields will be entered on checkout step 3.
Steps:
1. Open the cart and click Proceed to checkout.
2. If the wizard shows Sign in or Continue as Guest, stay signed in as the registered user (do not continue as guest).
3. On Billing Address, enter Country, Postal code, House number, Street, City, and State from TestData. Click Proceed to checkout when the button is enabled.
4. On Payment Method, select Cash on Delivery.
5. Click Confirm once. Wait until the payment check finishes (message or enabled state updates). Do not treat this click as order complete.
6. Click Confirm a second time.
7. Read the success view for an invoice number.
TestData:
Payment method: Cash on Delivery (cash-on-delivery)
Billing street: Test Street 1
Billing city: Utrecht
Billing state: Utrecht
Billing country: Austria (or the same country used at registration)
Billing postal code: 1234AA
Invoice rule: press Confirm twice on the UI (first click = payment check only; second click creates the invoice)
Wait between the two Confirm clicks; do not double-click immediately.
ExpectedResult:
Proceed to checkout on billing is disabled until the address is valid, then enabled.
First Confirm does not finish the order by itself (no final invoice as the only outcome of a single click).
After the second Confirm, a success/thank-you view shows an invoice number.
The payment method used is Cash on Delivery.
ActualResult: 2026-08-26. Mapped to tests/ui/purchase.spec.js @smoke @regression unique customer can search, update cart, checkout COD, and see invoice (Confirm twice). Passed.

Title: Single Confirm on COD checkout does not create an invoice
Preconditions: Logged in as a registered customer (TC-M-01). Cart has at least one product (add again if TC-M-06 emptied the cart). Open My invoices first and record the current invoice count and numbers. Start a fresh checkout; do not reuse a payment page that already received two Confirms.
Steps:
1. Open My invoices and record the current invoice count and numbers. Return to the shop.
2. Open the cart and click Proceed to checkout. Complete Billing Address with the same valid data as TC-M-06.
3. Select Payment Method Cash on Delivery.
4. Click Confirm exactly once.
5. Wait at least 5 seconds for the payment check to finish. Do not click Confirm again.
6. Observe whether a success view with a new invoice number appears.
7. Open My invoices again and compare with the list from step 1.
TestData:
Payment method: Cash on Delivery
Confirm clicks: 1 only (negative of the assessment Confirm-twice rule)
Wait: ≥5 seconds after the first Confirm
Do not immediately double-click Confirm (that can fire two payment checks and still create zero invoices, which is a different race).
ExpectedResult:
The tester remains on the payment step (or does not get a completed-order success with a new invoice number).
My invoices count and numbers are unchanged — no new invoice row is created.
This matches the UI quirk: the first Confirm only runs payment validation (/payment/check); the invoice is created on the second Confirm.
ActualResult: 2026-08-26. Mapped to tests/ui/purchase.spec.js @regression a single Confirm on COD checkout does not create an invoice. Passed.
